education.content:
Hendrik Bessembinder's 2018 study at Arizona State University examined 25,967 US stocks from 1926 to 2016. The finding: just 4% of listed stocks generated all net wealth creation above Treasury bills.

The other 96% collectively matched or underperformed one-month T-bills over their entire lifetimes.

This is why systematic screening matters. Finding the 4% is not about conviction or gut feel. It is about building a process that eliminates the 96% before capital is deployed. Our system rejected 99.9% of the universe last scan. That rejection rate is a feature.

Bessembinder, H. (2018). "Do Stocks Outperform Treasury Bills?" Journal of Financial Economics, 129(3), 440-457.

What does a stock look like the week before it triples?

We went back through 14 months of scanner signals. The pattern across our biggest winners ($SOFI +133%, $BAND +271%, $HIVE +114%): none of them looked exciting at entry.

Small companies. Under $20 per share. Analyst coverage of 2-4 firms at most. Volume below institutional radar. A structural force building underneath that most investors had not yet connected to the ticker.

The system does not look for excitement. It looks for accumulation in neglected corners of the market. By the time a stock is exciting, the best risk-reward is gone.

Position sizing determines outcomes more than stock selection.

A portfolio with one 300% winner and nine 20% losers breaks even at equal weight. The same portfolio with conviction-based sizing (20% in the winner, 5% in each loser) returns +42%.

Our system uses three tiers. Tier 1 positions get 2-3x the allocation of Tier 3. The difference is not opinion. It is measurable: catalyst proximity, structural force confirmation, downside protection from cash or assets on the balance sheet.

$BAND was sized as a small Tier 3 position at entry. Even at +271%, the portfolio-level contribution is proportional to the initial risk budget. Sizing protects on the way down. It compounds on the way up.

Most retail investors check their portfolios 4-7 times per day. A 2022 study by Vanguard's Investment Strategy Group found that investors who checked daily underperformed those who checked quarterly by 1.5 percentage points annually.

The mechanism is not information. It is emotion. Daily checking converts noise into decisions. A stock that drops 3% on no news triggers loss aversion. A stock that rises 5% triggers the disposition effect (sell winners too early).

Our system operates on weekly timeframes. Signals generate on Friday close. Exits trigger on weekly structural breaks, not intraday noise. The cadence is intentional.

Vanguard Investment Strategy Group (2022). "Frequency of Portfolio Review and Investor Outcomes."

scanner.content:
The last full screening: 1,279 tickers loaded. 30 showed momentum inflection. 54 confirmed trend acceleration. 18 cleared combined filters.

Three survived to full forensic analysis. All three from the same structural force: Biotech Capital Cycle Recovery.

One at conviction 8. One at conviction 7. One at conviction 6. The system sized them accordingly: largest allocation to the highest conviction, smallest to the lowest.

99.8% eliminated. Three deployed. That is selectivity.

This scan screened a cross-border payments company processing for six of the Magnificent Seven across 44 emerging markets. Revenue grew 47% to $1.09B. Forward P/E of 14.9x versus 39.5x fintech peer average.

We walked away.

No structural force alignment. Market cap 8x our system ceiling. The largest shareholder was actively selling. Conviction scores inflated between screening stages without material new findings to justify the upgrade.

Cheap and growing is not enough. The system requires force alignment, appropriate scale, and clean conviction trajectories. Three strikes.

Structural forces from the latest scan, ranked by composite quality:

Two PRIME (highest density of catalysts, confirmed capital flows): Navy submarine hardware manufacturing scored 8.75. CAR-T autoimmune scored 8.35. Both have 12-month funded pipelines and measurable institutional accumulation.

Three INVESTABLE (viable, need entry timing): CGT cold chain, EM payments infrastructure, 800G optical.

The scanner rejected 15 themes below quality threshold. Offshore oil restart, community banking, legacy media, home furnishings. Narrative without catalyst density.

thursday_education.topic: Investor Lessons: When the System Says Exit (KYTX Case Study)
thursday_education.prompt_instructions: Use Thursday Education prompt from Content Prompt Handbook v8.0, Rotation D (Investor Lessons), case_study subcategory. The lesson: systematic exits protect capital even when the fundamental thesis is correct. KYTX had successful clinical data, BLA filing proceeded, but the stock failed to confirm technically. Exit at -7.6% preserved capital for redeployment.

portfolio_context.original_thesis: Kyverna's miv-cel positioned to become first FDA-approved CAR-T therapy for autoimmune disease. Market implied 73% failure probability; we assigned 19%. 54pp gap on imminent BLA filing.
portfolio_context.what_happened: Clinical data was strong (all endpoints p<0.0001). BLA filing proceeded. But the stock failed to confirm the thesis technically. HMA exit triggered May 31.
portfolio_context.lesson: The system does not trade opinions. It trades confirmed momentum. When a stock fails to respond to positive catalysts, the signal tells you something the narrative cannot: capital is not flowing in. Exit discipline means accepting small losses instead of waiting for large ones.

voice_rules_reminders: Do not say 'HMA exit' or 'HMA pivot high'. Say 'systematic exit triggered' or 'exit criteria met'.
Frame the loss factually: '$KYTX at $9.22. Exited at $8.52. That is -7.6%.'
Do not say 'stopped out' or 'loss'. Say 'drawdown' or state factual P&L.
End with the forward lesson or redeployment implication.
